full_details: The morning loaf was still two fingers short. The two pounds stayed in the book until five. At two you played Egeon at the Theatre. The boxes were not counted. Between the play and the supper you put two pounds in the purse, and you had not heard whether the paper was granted. At six, at the Bell, Richard Quiney stood the wine because the brief is granted, which he was careful to separate from gathered. Before the capon was carved he put one pound on the board, in part of the two from August, and you counted one pound still owed. He made Henley Street better in the telling: your father on a ladder at the new barns, past sixty, and the men obeyed; the elder girl reading to the Sadlers of a Sunday; the younger asked twice at Hallowmas; the boy to Shottery and back while Quiney found his hat. After the capon you counted two pounds onto the board for the town and made him write the line. He asked ten pounds till Lady Day, for his own London charges, and said it was for the town. You gave the two to the town, lent nothing to the man, and told him you would still be friends at Lady Day. He drank your health. Before you left you wrote Anne six lines, to wait for the carrier of the fourth. At home the book took the two items and no new total.
one_sentence: You played Egeon, and at the Bell you gave two pounds to the brief and took one pound back.
title: Gave two pounds to the town
